root_cause.text: The L2CAP ECRED connection request handler did not verify that the command identifier was unique per signaling channel, allowing multiple requests with the same identifier to be accepted and marked as pending (FLAG_DEFER_SETUP), which could cause more than L2CAP_ECRED_MAX_CID channels to be allocated in l2cap_ecred_rsp_defer, leading to an array overflow.
root_cause.evidence: The commit adds a check using `__l2cap_chan_list_id(conn, cmd->ident, l2cap_ecred_list_defer, &num_scid)` to reject duplicate identifiers; the CVE description notes that without this check, multiple requests with the same identifier could be processed, causing an overflow when allocating CID values.

The group directly addresses the root cause by adding validation to reject duplicate ECRED connection requests with the same command identifier, which prevents the allocation of excessive channels that could lead to an array overflow.

candidates.rationale: This statement calculates the number of SCID channels from the command length without any upper bound or check against L2CAP_ECRED_MAX_CID, allowing an attacker to specify a large number of channels. Combined with the missing ident uniqueness check, multiple requests with the same identifier can accumulate channels, leading to array overflow in l2cap_ecred_rsp_defer.

vuln_statements.explanation: This statement calculates the number of SCID channels from the command length without any upper bound or check against L2CAP_ECRED_MAX_CID. Combined with the missing identifier uniqueness verification (allowing multiple requests with the same identifier to be accepted and marked as pending), an attacker can cause more channels to be allocated than the fixed-size array can hold, leading to an array overflow in l2cap_ecred_rsp_defer.
